brief:
A simple trip across Gaza to purchase za'atar, a common herb used in Palestinian cuisine, now requires residents to make a series of life-or-death decisions, We Are Not Numbers reported. The routine errand exemplifies how ordinary travel has become perilous, forcing Palestinians to navigate routes transformed by conflict and calculate which paths offer the safest passage.

The conditions across Gaza have fundamentally altered daily life, turning even basic commerce into an act requiring careful risk assessment. Residents must constantly evaluate when and where to venture out to meet essential needs, as roads have become dangerous territory where a trip to buy groceries or spices carries grave consequences for personal safety.
dek: A simple trip across Gaza to share some za’atar requires a series of life-or-death decisions.
title: Gazans weigh survival against necessity on dangerous daily journeys
